headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from Dify’s shared datastore and file/tool surfaces; RisingWave adds no compensating ingress controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and uses shared state via the Dify server datastore, so attacker-controlled content can reach agent logic. RisingWave has no documented input channel here, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Dify workflows read uploaded files or datastore entries as instructions without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF RisingWave outputs are manually copied into Dify, the bridge becomes stronger.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all retrieved content.
Disable instruction-following from retrieved files.
Separate user content from system prompts in Dify.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing.
Run a quick red-team prompt-injection test on one workflow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, and its shared datastore can expose data across instances. RisingWave is documented as network-egress none, so it is not the leak source; the risk is Dify-side leakage of sensitive workspace data into shared state or logs.
conditions: IF multiple Dify instances share the same datastore namespace, conversation logs may cross boundaries.
IF knowledge-base files contain sensitive data, they can be retained in shared state or logs.
mitigations: Restrict Dify datastore access to one tenant.
Purge old conversation logs.
Move sensitive KB files to a separate workspace.
requires-engineering: encrypt shared datastore at rest with tenant keys.
Verify RisingWave remains network-isolated in deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad filesystem write and shell/subprocess execution, while RisingWave is documented only as a non-networking data-engineering component with no write surface shown. No shared mutable resource or overlapping write target is documented, so a direct capability conflict is possible only under unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory or database, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps Dify tool output into RisingWave-managed state, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources.
Use file locks for any shared artifact.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state.
Check deployment manifests for overlapping mounts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can produce tool outputs and workflow results that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. RisingWave is a data-engineering system, so if its pipeline consumes Dify output without verification, errors can cascade into stored or transformed data. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests Dify-generated records without validation, bad facts can propagate.
IF Dify workflows emit unverified citations or structured data, downstream transformations may amplify errors.
mitigations: Add schema validation before ingestion.
Require human review for high-impact records.
Tag Dify outputs as untrusted.
requires-engineering: implement end-to-end provenance checks.
Sample one pipeline run and compare against source data.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, model-provider API keys, and tool credentials, which can create retention and residency obligations. RisingWave’s profile does not show regulated data handling or a conflicting residency regime, so only Dify-side compliance gaps are evident here.
conditions: IF conversation logs contain regulated data, retention policy must be enforced.
IF knowledge-base files include personal data, deletion/export handling must be defined.
mitigations: Review Dify retention settings.
Exclude regulated data from KB uploads.
Document deletion/export procedures.
requires-engineering: add residency controls and DPA review.
Audit secret storage locations.
